column1: # Terminology data that is NOT in the git checkout, and where to get it.
# These three used to be tracked here through Git LFS. Nothing the wheel ships
# reads them — `scripts/check_wheel_data.py` has forbidden all three since
# 1.3.0 — and together they were 29 MB that every `git clone` paid for over
# LFS, which is the slow half of cloning this repository.
# `scripts/fetch_data.sh` reads this file. `./deploy.sh` calls it for the
# `runtime` rows; pass `--all` for the `build` rows too.
# The checksum is each file's Git LFS object id, because git-lfs names objects
# by their sha256 — so a download can be checked against the history the file
# came from, not just against this table.
# To publish a new version: upload to a new `data-YYYY-MM-DD` release, then
# change RELEASE and the rows below in one commit. Old deployments keep
# working; they pin the tag they were checked out with.
# columns: name <TAB> sha256 <TAB> bytes <TAB> need <TAB> what reads it
#   need = runtime  a deployment wants it; deploy.sh fetches it
#   need = build    only the bundle-build passes read it
#   need = archive  nothing reads it any more; kept so an older tag resolves
RELEASE
# 1.5.0 reads NONE of these. The semantic tier that opened the concept graph
# was deleted with `mirobody/indicator/`, and the bundle is now cut straight
# from a LOINC release by `translate_build/`, which reads `Loinc.csv` and the
# LinguisticVariants files and nothing here. They stay listed, with `need =
# archive`, so the checksums that name them survive and an older deployment
# pinned to its own tag keeps working; `fetch_data.sh` no longer downloads
# them. Delete the rows once no supported version wants them.
fhir_concept_graph.bin
fhir_meta.csv.gz
